Choosing a finish shouldn’t be guesswork

A floor finish is a visual decision. Compare all six systems side by side — what each one looks like, where it works hardest — then carry your pick straight into the quote builder.

Garage Flake

Vinyl flakes broadcast into a tinted base and sealed under a clear topcoat. The speckled finish shrugs off dust and daily wear and turns a garage into a clean, finished room.

Look
Speckled, textured
Sheen
Satin to gloss
Best for
Garages, workshops, hobby bays

Six systems. One right floor.

Every service Epoxy Guys offers, shown the way it actually looks on the ground — so the conversation starts from a finish you’ve already seen.

Garage Flake

Full-broadcast vinyl flake over a tinted base, sealed clear. Hides dust, adds grip, and makes a garage sweep-out simple.

Garages · Workshops · Hobby bays

Metallic Epoxy

Pigments worked into clear resin while wet, so every floor cures with its own flowing, marble-like movement. No two are alike.

Showrooms · Retail · Statement garages

Overlays

A thin cement-based layer resurfaces worn concrete and takes stain, texture, or stone patterns — a new surface without tearing out the slab.

Patios · Entries · Worn concrete

Micro Cement

Hand-troweled in thin layers for a seamless, mineral finish with soft movement — a quiet, architectural look for interiors.

Kitchens · Baths · Boutiques

Quartz Broadcast

Colored quartz granules broadcast into resin build a dense, textured surface with strong grip — a workhorse where floors get wet.

Locker rooms · Commercial kitchens · Labs

Urethane Cement

A heavy-duty cementitious system built for thermal shock, hot washdowns, and constant moisture in working plants.

Food & beverage plants · Breweries · Kitchens

Commercial & industrial, presented like it matters

Warehouses, plants, and commercial spaces are the core of the work — so they lead the page, not a photo of a garage.

Warehouses & shops

Seamless epoxy systems with safety striping that keep large floors cleanable, bright, and easy to read at a glance.

Food & beverage

Urethane cement where hot washdowns, moisture, and thermal shock are part of the daily routine.

Retail & showrooms

Metallic and quartz systems that make the floor part of the presentation, not an afterthought.
